newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt welcomes court OK on resort.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt welcomes court OK on resort.

text.p: Australian Environment Minister Robert Hill on Friday welcomed a court dismissal of a challenge to his decision to allow construction of a controversial tourist resort.

Hill said the Federal Court's decision confirmed he had exercised his ministerial responsibilities properly when he ruled development of the A$100 million Port Hinchinbrook resort in far north Queensland state posed no environmental threat.
"The decision of the court vindicates the rigorous process the government undertook before granting consent," Hill told reporters.
"We recognise that we now have an ongoing responsibility to ensure that work on the development proceeds within the terms of the deed of agreement."
Earlier on Friday, the court ruled Hill acted correctly when he followed advice which led him to approve the project.

In August last year, environmental group the Friends of Hinchinbrook Society challenged the minister's decision, saying he had improperly exercised his powers under the World Heritage Act and made a number of legal errors in giving his approval.
